statement:
For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

For a directed system of ring maps $(A_i\to B_i)$, let $A=\varinjlim A_i$ and $B=\varinjlim B_i$. When comparing $L_{B_i/A_i}$ over the different rings $B_i$, use the transition maps to view their filtered colimit as a complex over $B$. Filtered colimits of modules are exact and commute with polynomial algebra formation and Kähler differentials.

Let $A_i \to B_i$ be a system of ring maps over a directed index
set $I$. Then, with the filtered colimit taken using the functorial transition maps and viewed as a complex of $\varinjlim B_i$-modules, $\varinjlim_i L_{B_i/A_i}\simeq L_{\varinjlim_i B_i/\varinjlim_i A_i}$.

\label{lemma-polynomial}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $A \to B$ be a finite type ring map.
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the category of $A$-algebra maps $C \to B$. Let
$n \geq 0$ and let $P_\bullet$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal{A}$
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $P_\bullet \to B$ is a trivial Kan fibration of simplicial sets,
\item $P_k$ is finite type over $A$ for $k \leq n$,
\item $P_\bullet = \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n P_\bullet$ as simplicial
objects of $\mathcal{A}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $P_{n + 1}$ is a finite type $A$-algebra.

Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $A \to B$ be a finite type ring map.
There exists a simplicial $A$-algebra $P_\bullet$ with an augmentation
$\epsilon : P_\bullet \to B$ such that each $P_n$ is a polynomial algebra
of finite type over $A$ and such that $\epsilon$ is a trivial
Kan fibration of simplicial sets.

\label{lemma-special-case}
Let $A = \mathbf{Z}[x_1, \ldots, x_n] \to B = \mathbf{Z}$
be the ring map which sends $x_i$ to $0$ for $i = 1, \ldots, n$.

statement:
For a ring map $A\to B$, let $\Omega_{B/A}$ be the module of Kähler differentials. The cotangent complex $L_{B/A}\in D(B)$ is obtained from the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra resolution $P_\bullet\to B$, where $P_0=A[B]$, $P_1=A[A[B]]$, etc., by taking the chain complex (in nonpositive cohomological degrees) associated to the simplicial $B$-module $\Omega_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B$. Here $A[E]$ denotes the polynomial algebra freely generated by a set $E$, $D(B)$ is the derived category of $B$-modules, and $H^i$ denotes degree-$i$ cohomology.

A quasi-isomorphism is a map of complexes inducing an isomorphism on every cohomology module. We write $M[0]$ for a module concentrated in degree zero, $M[1]$ for a module in degree $-1$, $\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}$ for derived tensor product, and $\tau_{\geq -1}$ for the standard truncation in cohomological degrees at least $-1$. The module $\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by symbols $db$ subject to additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $da=0$ for $a\in A$.

An ordered sequence $(f_1,\dots,f_r)$ in a ring $A$ is Koszul-regular if the Koszul complex $K(f_1,\dots,f_r;A)$ has no positive-degree homology. A Koszul ideal is locally generated by a Koszul-regular sequence. A local complete intersection (lci) ring map $A\to B$ locally factors as a smooth algebra map followed by a quotient whose kernel is generated by a regular sequence. A perfect complex is locally quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules; Tor-amplitude in $[-1,0]$ means its derived tensor product with any module has cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$.

\label{lemma-tensor-product-tor-independent}
If $A$ and $B$ are Tor independent $R$-algebras, then the object $E$
in (\ref{equation-tensor-product}) is zero. In this case we have
$$
L_{A \otimes_R B/R} =
L_{A/R} \otimes_A^\mathbf{L} (A \otimes_R B) \oplus
L_{B/R} \otimes_B^\mathbf{L} (A \otimes_R B)
$$
which is represented by the complex
$L_{A/R} \otimes_R B \oplus L_{B/R} \otimes_R A $
of $A \otimes_R B$-modules.
